title: Redwood discovery - model selection (Lighthouse AI)
summary: Discovery focused on model choice for Lighthouse AI: they need long context for multi-doc summarization, robust multilingual support, and tool-calling for retrieval and DB ops. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, SOC2/KMS concerns, and running benchmarks. Agreed next steps: send sizing/pricing, share security pack, run a 2-week pilot on dedicated capacity with model A/B tests.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Devon Lee (Redwood SE), Marcus Chen (CTO - Lighthouse AI), Priya Nair (ML Eng), Omar Reyes (Infra), Leah Park (PM)

[00:00] Samira (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Samira from Redwood, Devon our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:08] Marcus (CTO): Doing well, Marcus here. Thanks for setting this up. We sent a calendar invite as lighthouse-model-selection.
[00:12] Priya (ML Eng): Priya joining — we'll jump in on model questions.
[00:15] Omar (Infra): Omar here, I'll cover infra/security.
[00:20] Samira (AE): Awesome. Goal for today: understand your workload (context length, multilingual, tool-calling), and give model recommendations and deployment options — hosted vs dedicated vs private. We'll capture those and propose a pilot. Sound good?
[00:30] Leah (PM): Yep, that's the plan.

---
[00:45] Devon (SE): Quick high level from our side: Redwood supports hosted API for quick integration, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and Private for VPC/on-prem. For model selection we look at model family, context window, tokenization quirks for languages, and tool-calling primitives.
[01:05] Marcus (CTO): High level context: our product ingests multiple long legal and financial docs per user session, then generates summarizations and Q&A across combined docs. Typical session is 10-20 docs, cumulative tokens often 80k-120k, sometimes peaks to 250k for enterprise customers.
[01:30] Priya (ML Eng): We also need multi-lingual support — English plus Spanish, French, Portuguese, and some Chinese and Japanese. Accuracy in non-English is a must.
[01:45] Devon (SE): Got it. So long-context is the priority. We usually recommend a hybrid approach: for the bulk we do retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with embeddings + a long-context model for final synthesis, or context window models with KV cache and prefixing.
[02:05] Omar (Infra): We're also very strict on data residency and KMS control — any private deployment needs to support our KMS for key wrapping, and audit logs for all inference requests. SOC 2 is minimal; some customers need ISO as well.

---
[02:30] Samira (AE): On vendor landscape, are you evaluating any competitors right now?
[02:35] Marcus (CTO): We're looking at OpenAI endpoints for speed, Anthropic in some safety tests, and self-hosting using on-prem clusters potentially via Vertex AI or pure EC2 instances. Cohere came up in a proof of concept too.
[02:50] Samira (AE): Good to know. We'll mention how Redwood differentiates: production-first runtime with batching and KV cache, and the ability to route requests to cheaper quantized variants or fall back to hosted models.

---
[03:10] Devon (SE): For your token counts, we have two main options: 1) Redwood Hosted with models that support very long context windows (we have curated open models with ~64k windows and some experimental 128k ones), or 2) Dedicated/Private where you can run custom compiled kernels and use sequence-slicing + KV cache to effectively handle 200k+ logical tokens across retrieval. The tradeoff is cost and control. Hosted is faster to try; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale; Private gives full network control and KMS integration.
[03:45] Priya (ML Eng): Are there open models that natively do 200k? I thought most open models top out at 64k.
[03:55] Devon (SE): Most off-the-shelf open models are 32k-64k. For 200k we typically layer retrieval and chunking, plus Redwood's KV cache to stitch context. There's some newer long-context variants (LLaMA-... long, Mistral long-context forks) but they're experimental. For tight latency and native long context, sometimes a hybrid where we keep embeddings + condensed context is more stable. Also model quantization is important for Dedicated to reduce memory.
[04:25] Marcus (CTO): Tool-calling — we need to call our vector DB and internal tools (search, internal DB writes) from the model. How mature is your tool-calling?
[04:35] Devon (SE): We support function/tool calling style patterns. Hosted API supports tool calls with structured JSON responses and secure webhook routing. For Dedicated/Private we provide interfaces to run tool hooks internally; Private can keep all calls inside VPC. There have been occasional transcription hiccups where tool names are garbled in auto-transcripts, but functionally it's supported.
[04:55] Omar (Infra): Important: any outbound webhook must be allowed via our egress policy, or we prefer the model to call an internal stub that you host inside our VPC. Is that supported?
[05:05] Devon (SE): Yes — with Private we can install a small connector inside your network to proxy tool calls and keep traffic internal. For Dedicated we can also deploy in customer's cloud region with VPC peering. Hosted can be configured with private network options but will require stricter agreements.

---
[05:25] Priya (ML Eng): On multilingual: do you have recommended models that perform well on Spanish/Portuguese and also Asian languages? We've seen big gaps in Chinese/Japanese.
[05:35] Devon (SE): We generally recommend ensemble testing. There are multilingual variants (mT5-like, GPT-J variants tuned multilingual) and some community checkpoints fine-tuned for non-western languages. Redwood's Optimize tooling can run automatic evals on your language prompt set and surface model-by-language performance. For production we recommend a primary model that handles most langs and a fallback per-language for tricky cases.
[05:55] Marcus (CTO): So practically, what does pilot look like?
[06:00] Samira (AE): Typical pilot: 2 weeks. We provision a small Dedicated pool or Hosted with a committed burst capacity, we ingest your sample dataset, run a model A/B with 2 model families (e.g., Model A: long-context open variant + RAG; Model B: medium-context higher-quality open model with heavier reranking), and we report on latency, token cost, and quality metrics you care about.
[06:25] Leah (PM): That matches what we wanted. Who from your side runs the benchmark?
[06:30] Devon (SE): We'll run the harness with your prompts; we ask you to supply the prompt set and sample docs. We'll instrument with Redwood Console dashboards so you can see per-route costs, latency percentiles, and token breakdown.

---
[06:45] Marcus (CTO): Security checklist — we need SOC2, SSO (SAML/Okta), RBAC, plaintext logs retention policy, and KMS integration. Does Redwood support bring-your-own-key (BYOK)?
[07:00] Devon (SE): Yes. For Private and Dedicated we support KMS integrations and BYOK; Hosted supports customer-managed keys in some regions depending on compliance package. Audit logs and per-token traceability are available in the Console. We'll share our security pack (SOC2 reports, ISO summary) after the call.
[07:20] Omar (Infra): Also need to understand data retention on hosted endpoints — how long are prompts and outputs stored?
[07:28] Samira (AE): By default Redwood stores logs for 30 days for troubleshooting, but we have enterprise retention controls and can disable retention for certain routes. We'll include that in the security doc.

---
[07:40] Priya (ML Eng): Latency: for interactive users we need median latency under 350ms for short prompts and under 2s for synthesis. What’s realistic for a 4k-8k window model?
[07:55] Devon (SE): For 4k-8k open models on Dedicated GPU pools you can expect sub-second median for generation up to some token limits; large long-context models will have higher latency. Batching and continuous KV cache help with throughput. We'll need to test with your actual prompts; that's what the pilot is for.
[08:10] Marcus (CTO): Cost: what's unit cost difference hosted vs dedicated? Rough numbers ok.
[08:15] Samira (AE): Hosted has higher unit cost due to managed infra; Dedicated reduces per-token cost significantly at commit levels. Private is similar to Dedicated but with platform license. We'll send a sizing sheet with sample unit economics comparing options.

---
[08:35] Devon (SE): Quick note on quantization: on Dedicated we can run int8/int4 quantized variants which reduces GPU memory and cost but can slightly affect quality. For multilingual or subtle tasks we often suggest evaluating quantized vs fp16 variants. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles by workload.
[08:55] Priya (ML Eng): Good — please include quantization guidance in the doc.

---
[09:05] Samira (AE): Any blockers on your side for starting a pilot?
[09:10] Marcus (CTO): We need approval from legal for any data transfer, and we'll confirm internal budget. Also Omar needs to confirm KMS policy. Otherwise timeline looks like mid-March for pilot.
[09:20] Leah (PM): We'll prioritize the sample data and prompt list; expect that by Monday.

---
[09:30] Devon (SE): I'll attach a checklist and starter prompt set after this call. For model candidates for the A/B: Model A (64k long-context open variant, quantized) with RAG; Model B (48k higher-quality variant + reranker). We'll try both on english and top languages.
[09:50] Priya (ML Eng): Any specific model names? You mentioned some Llama variants and Mistral forks earlier — can you list them in the follow-up?
[09:58] Devon (SE): Yes, we'll list specific checkpoints (community long-LLaMA variants, Mistral long forks, and some tuned multilingual open checkpoints). We'll also note tradeoffs per language.

---
[10:12] Omar (Infra): One more infra detail: for Private deployment do you support on-prem air-gapped installs? We have a few customers requiring that.
[10:20] Devon (SE): Yes, Private can be on-prem with an air-gapped install. It needs some prep for model weights provisioning and key exchange; we'll include the runbook in the security package.

---
[10:35] Samira (AE): Recap and next steps: Samira sends pricing and committed capacity options; Devon sends benchmark guide, model candidate list, and prompt template; Marcus and team provide sample data and language priorities; then we schedule a 2-week pilot week of 2026-03-16. We'll also share SOC2/security docs and KMS integration notes.
[10:55] Marcus (CTO): Great, thanks. Looks reasonable.
[11:00] Leah (PM): One more ask — include an example of function/tool calling payloads for DB writes.
[11:05] Devon (SE): Will do — example webhook schema and internal stub pattern included.

---
[11:15] Samira (AE): Thanks everyone; we'll follow up with the materials.
[11:20] Marcus (CTO): Thanks.
[11:22] End of recording.

Notes: transcript contains small transcription artifacts (model names sometimes truncated; 'K V cache' written as 'KV cash' in one segment). Shared artifacts: Pricing sheet (link: https://redwood.example.com/decks/lighthouse-pricing), Security pack (link: https://redwood.example.com/security/lighthouse-pack), Benchmark guide (link: https://redwood.example.com/harnesses/lighthouse-guide).
